market: LAR −4.5, total 47.5. Stafford 33 attempts / 22.5 completions; Daniels 30.5 / 19.5 and 6.5 rushes. Kyren Williams 13.5 carries; Corum 11.5.
lineup: LAR is without WR2 Davante Adams (out since Week 7), TE Terrance Ferguson (out) and CB Jaylen Watson (out); TE Colby Parkinson and WR Jordan Whittington are questionable. Daniels is healthy after missing Weeks 3–4. WAS has a new OC, David Blough, and Daniels has said he wants to avoid the hits that cost him 10 games in 2025.

keys.take: Puka Nacua, who has had 34% and 48% target shares since Adams went down.
keys.how: Blitz. WAS sends extra rushers on 43.6% of dropbacks, the most of any defense this week.
keys.gives: Hot reads and quick slants, Nacua's routes. WAS allows 19.1 WR targets and 149 WR yards a game.
keys.counter: Stafford gets it out to Nacua before the blitz arrives. In LAR's two wins without Adams he threw 25–29 times and Nacua still caught 8 and 11.

keys.how: Rush four and keep him in the pocket (LAR blitzes 29.3%). LAR forces QBs out of the pocket on only 19% of dropbacks.
keys.gives: Time for Daniels to throw (300 yards against SF).
keys.counter: Daniels scrambles when the coverage holds. Nearly all his rushing yards come from scrambles (7 of 8 runs in his 104-yard game).

scripts.control: LAR leads. Stafford's attempts fall to the 25–29 range, but Nacua's share rises without Adams. WAS throws, and Daniels' scrambles depend on whether LAR's rush flushes him.
scripts.competitive: LAR's close games averaged 48 attempts, and Nacua's catch ceiling is in double digits (17 against BUF).
scripts.reversal: WAS leads on the ground. Daniels slides early and protects himself, the opposite of a rushing-over game. Nacua's volume goes up as LAR chases.

plays.why: His rushing has become scramble-only, the scrambles are falling, and the healthy version of Daniels is throwing first under a new OC.
plays.support: Play-by-play: zero designed runs in his last two games (3 and 2 scrambles, for 11 and 23 yards). NFL.com (Shook, spring): Daniels wants to avoid the hits that cost him 10 games in 2025.
plays.sample: 40+ in 2 of 5 starts, both before Week 6 (69 against DAL, 104 against NYG on mostly scrambles).
plays.counter: If LAR's rush flushes him, one 30-yard scramble cashes the Yes. WAS is the underdog, and chasing games are when he's run most.
plays.loses: WAS trails and Daniels improvises (the NYG game: 7 scrambles), or one long run.
plays.vs: Preferred over under 50 (No 69¢, needs 71%), which is safer but priced past what the sample supports.

plays.why: WAS's blitz-heavy plan meets a QB who has funneled 34–48% of his targets to one receiver since Adams went down.
plays.support: WAS blitzes 43.6% (most here) and allows 19.1 WR targets a game. Nacua's share is 34% for the season and 48% last week.
plays.sample: 8+ catches in 4 of 6, including both games without Adams (8 and 11).
plays.counter: LAR's wins came on 25–29 attempts, and a quiet blowout could leave him at 6 or 7.
plays.loses: LAR leads by 14 at half and runs Kyren and Corum, or WAS doubles Nacua and forces Higbee to beat it.
plays.vs: Beat 9+ (45¢, needs 47%), which has a higher ceiling but loses to a normal 8-catch game, and 7+ (71¢), which is too expensive.

passed.name: Matthew Stafford 275+ pass yds (34¢)
passed.why: His volume swings with the script (25–29 attempts in wins, 51–54 in close games). At 34¢ the price is fair either way.

passed.name: Kyren Williams 3+ rec (55¢)
passed.why: WAS allows 6.9 RB targets a game, but Kyren has had 1–3 targets in each of the last three games.
passed.move: Parkinson and Higbee limited, so backs run more of the hot routes.

passed.name: WSH running backs
passed.why: A Rachaad White / Ekeler / Croskey-Merritt split.
passed.move: A beat report on the carry plan.
